title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter ordering and token/event framing in streaming responses
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: multiple customers and internal e2e tests observed malformed partial-JSON objects and out-of-order token/event delimiter emissions when using SSE streaming with long messages, tool-calling and structured output. This caused downstream consumers (OpenAI-compatible clients, SDKs) to fail JSON-parsing or to reassemble events incorrectly under high-concurrency conditions. This PR fixes the delimiter ordering bug and token/event framing edge-cases by: 1) unifying the framing state machine for chunk boundaries so delimiter tokens ("[DELIM]") are emitted only after preceding token frames are flushed; 2) introducing a compact sequence number in the event envelope to ensure deterministic reassembly on client side; 3) hardening partial-JSON emission so incomplete JSON fragments never include trailing commas or mismatched braces; 4) adding a defensive recovery path that emits an explicit "event: error" with metadata when a framing inconsistency is detected to aid SDKs in graceful fallback. Changes are backward-compatible with our OpenAI compatibility layer (we maintain the same top-level fields and stream envelopes), and include a compatibility flag for older clients. Checklist: - [x] Reproduce failure in perf-canary harness (included reproducer) - [x] Add unit tests for framing state transitions - [x] Add integration test with redwood-sdk-python streaming parser - [x] Add e2e sanity test for tool/function-calling flows with structured JSON output - [x] Update CHANGELOG and release notes. Impact: fixes multiple customer-facing flakes for streaming responses, improves stability for tool-calling and structured output, negligible latency impact (~0.3ms median on microbenchmarks). Related: referenced flaky incident INT-981 (internal) and follow-ups to PRs pr-21458, pr-202341 and pr-152999. Note: this was validated on Dedicated and Hosted runtimes, and toggled behind a runtime feature flag until the rollout completed.

review_conversation: Rohit Malhotra (reviewer): Can you walk through how sequence numbers interact with the existing KV cache streaming optimization? Concerned about extra metadata overhead.

Ava Martinez (author): Sequence number is compact (uint16) and only added to event envelope, it doesn't affect KV cache contents; added microbenchmarks showing negligible overhead. See commit a1b2c3d.
Janelle Park (reviewer): The integration test flakes in CI were because the SDK parser expects a trailing newline after final event. Can we normalize that?
Ava Martinez (author): Normalized final-event emission to include a terminating newline; added test to lock behavior. See commit d4e5f6a.
Diego Alvarez (reviewer): Please add a release note and mark compatibility flag so we can rollout gradually for Dedicated customers.
Ava Martinez (author): Added release notes and runtime flag. Rolling out under feature flag sse.strict_framing.
